note:
FOUR FILES IN THE REPOSITORY, THREE OF THEM IN THE CONTAINER, and the difference is a MODEL CHOICE rather than a packer's. The repository monkt/paddleocr-onnx ships TWO text detectors -- detection/v3/det.onnx (2.3 MB, MobileNetV3 + SCSE) and detection/v5/det.onnx (84 MB) -- and ONE recogniser per language. The v3 detector is the one this container holds, because it is 36 times smaller and 14 times faster on the frame below; the v5 is a separate network, not a variant of it, and the packer REFUSES a directory that holds both by name (tools/pack/pack_npue.py: 'holds 2 detectors'), because picking the wrong one silently is a different network with different accuracy. Its sha256 is 61824840edf6e74581898930b8091b1b2318f4b2705a2e8a40ad3de7ac480133, and the same runtime packs it when the file is named directly with --ocr-det. The v3 detector's is ee40e80071ba3a320d4efda75f3e22047a7d049e9bf7bcaaf9daea23fc21b935.

MEASURED, both detectors, same runtime, same frame: the v5's boxes are 8 to 12 px WIDER than the v3's on all three lines -- its probability map is at a quarter of the resolution, so the un-clip expands a coarser box -- and its detector takes 11253 ms against the v3's 800 ms. All three TRANSCRIPTIONS ARE IDENTICAL either way, which is the point worth keeping: the detector's resolution changes where the text is, not what it says.

THE THREE FILES ARE ONE MODEL, for the same reason arch=7's palm detector and arch=8's person detector are in their containers: a detector finds text and cannot read it, and a recogniser reads a crop and cannot find one, so a container holding only one of them answers 'no text here' to every image. The dictionary is the third file for the same reason: the recogniser's head emits 438 classes and the dictionary holds 436 characters, and a recogniser read with the wrong one transcribes English text into confidently wrong characters -- the CTC table is the dictionary's lines plus 'blank' first and ' ' last.

THE DICTIONARY IS NOT A WORD LIST AND NOT A VOCABULARY FILE: it is 436 lines, one character each, and the ORDER matters, because the class index IS the line number. It carries no space at all -- the recogniser's 438 classes are the 436 lines plus 'blank' FIRST and ' ' LAST, and the decoder adds those two rather than the file, so that there is one place that decides what a blank is and it is not the file. The file ends with a newline, and reading it with a trailing-newline mishandling shifts the whole table by one, which produces text that is confidently wrong rather than an error.

MEASURED against rapidocr-onnxruntime 1.2.3, which is the reference implementation this tree's algorithm follows, on docs/ocr_text.png (900x360, three lines of text, GoogleSansFlex at 56 px): the three boxes agree to within 4 px and ALL THREE TRANSCRIPTIONS ARE IDENTICAL -- 'Hello OCR World', 'NpuEmbeddings 12345' and 'PaddleOCR on AMD NPU'. The reference's own pipeline on the same frame gives the same three strings. tools/verify/verify_ocr.py is the gate and it has four sections: the packed op list against onnxruntime op by op (153 detector ops, 334 recogniser ops, worst 2.6e-07 of peak), the runtime's walk against an independent reading of the op list (155 and 3x335 nodes), the runtime end to end against rapidocr, and the array path against the host path on the same frame.

THE FLOAT VARIANT IS THE ONLY VARIANT, and the reason is a LAYOUT rather than a precision. The quantisation path stores a convolution's weight as an [N, K] view with one scale per output channel, and the DB head's two TRANSPOSED convolutions are laid out the other way round -- [Cin, Cout, kh, kw], the input channels first -- so a quantised container would carry a 24-number scale sidecar for a 1-channel weight, which the runtime refuses to load. tools/pack/packers/ocr.py refuses --dtype i8 and --dtype i4 BY NAME and says why; --dtype bf16 works and gives the same three strings with the boxes within 1 px.

THE IMAGE is not in the repository: it is docs/ocr_text.png, made for this tree, because models/** is gitignored except this file and a golden's image beside a container would exist only where it was recorded. Its sha256 is above so a substitute cannot be used silently. The licence is Apache-2.0, which the repository's own model card states.
